The test image shows very young seedlings (cotyledon stage) that are wilting, collapsing, and dying near the soil line — with tan/brown soft-looking stems and overall plant collapse. This is classic damping-off pattern.

Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off** (water-soaked, soft rot, collapsed seedlings) or **Rhizoctonia** (sunken brown lesion at soil line, "wire stem"). The soft collapsing without a distinct sunken lesion points more toward Pythium. Let me confirm with a reference.

The reference confirms Pythium damping-off: brown/tan hypocotyl decay at the seedling stage causing collapse. The test image matches well — multiple young seedlings collapsed/wilting near the soil line with tan-brown soft stem tissue, in sandy soil conditions typical for Pythium infection.
